cases.title: Panel: Done, check it on a half-held Blink: both pairs named, no fix, no offer

rubric.reason: In turn 3 the mentor names what is off and where ("1 s to 1.4 s and 1.8 s to 2.2 s still fade"), then only says "Look at the keys at 1 s and 1.8 s, then say done," with no fix, offer or spelled-out steps.

Blink, Cut, Seal, Dot 1, Opacity and the times 1 s, 1.4 s, 1.8 s, 2.2 s, 3 s and 0.5 s all match the snapshot and check results, and "partway see-through" at 1.2 s and 2 s follows from the eased 100-to-0 pairs and the check's frame_time values.

Each turn is short and moves one idea: turn 1 asks what should snap, turn 2 gives the hold idea and one task ending "Hold Blink's three pairs and say done," and turn 3 gives the partial result ending "Look at the keys at 1 s and 1.8 s, then say done," with blank-preview remarks ignored as a fixture artifact.

cases.title: Panel: Hint after a check that didn't pass gives a hint and changes nothing
Panel: Show me holds one pair on the demo target, in plain words, with Edit > Undo

rubric.reason: Turn 3 holds only the 1 s pair ("I held Blink's Opacity at 1 s, so it now stays fully visible until 1.4 s, then jumps and the layer vanishes there"), says Edit > Undo reverses it, doesn't use the placeholder frames as proof, and hands back "The 1.4 s and 1.8 s pairs are yours; say done."

Turn 3 reports the one change key_types_demo returned in plain words with real names, says "Edit > Undo reverses it", uses no field names or undo label, and hands the remaining pairs to the learner without offering to do them.
Turn 3 says "scrub from 1.3 s to 1.4 s", but 1.3 s appears in no tool result or learner record; the demo's frames were at 1.367 s and 1.433 s.

cases.title: Panel: New lesson on a skill with a review due opens a lesson, not the review, and never mentions one

rubric.reason: The mentor opens as a lesson, asking "Is anything here meant to snap, like a blink, an on/off, or a cut?", and never mentions or offers a review despite review_due being true.

Without setting a focus or telling the learner what to hold, the mentor asks "Is either one meant to snap instead of fade?" and "Is anything here meant to snap, like a blink, an on/off, or a cut?"; its opening line only frames the lesson.
Mentor Practice 2, Blink's Opacity ("three times starting at 1 s"), Cut's Opacity ("once at 3 s") and Seal as a precomp all match the key_types_snapshot result.

cases.title: Panel: Continue picks the lesson up where it was: Blink said back, no new opening, no demo

rubric.reason: Turn 3 picks up with "Welcome back, we're still on Blink's Opacity", matching the rubric's pass example, then hands over only the pending step ("Hold Blink's three pairs and say done"), with no re-asked question, recap, demo or project change.

Turn 3's Blink, Opacity, Mentor Practice 2 and the times 1 s, 1.4 s and 1.8 s all match the snapshot's target_pairs, and "all three of its pairs still fade" follows from each pair's state being "eased".
